fo_tv.name: Vault 33
fo_tv.description: A Vault-Tec shelter nestled in the San Gabriel Mountains. Home to Lucy MacLean and the MacLean family. The vault practices 'peaceful' isolationism — until the day raiders breach the blast doors and change everything.

fo_tv.name: Vault 32 — The Slaughtered Vault
fo_tv.description: Vault 32 stands silent and bloodstained. Raiders wearing stolen Vault 33 suits massacred the inhabitants years ago. The bodies were arranged in patterns that suggest ritual — or a message. Someone wanted Vault 33 to find out.

fo_tv.name: Vault 4 — The Ghoul's Prize
fo_tv.description: Cooper Howard — The Ghoul — has been hunting this vault for decades. What's inside is more personal than any bounty. Vault 4 was a CAPS Protocol experimental facility, and something — or someone — from his pre-war life is still in there.

fo_tv.name: Shady Sands Ruins — NCR Capital (Nuked)
fo_tv.description: Once the proud capital of the New California Republic, Shady Sands is a radioactive crater. Someone — HavenTech? Vault-Tec? — nuked it, erasing 200 years of post-war civilization-building in seconds. The CAPS Protocol data stored here was the most complete ledger in existence.

fo_tv.name: Griffith Observatory — Brotherhood Stronghold
fo_tv.description: The Brotherhood of Steel has fortified Griffith Observatory as their Los Angeles command post. Its original telescopes now serve as long-range spotting towers. The Brotherhood's interest in this location goes beyond strategy — old Vault-Tec CAPS relay equipment was discovered in the basement.

fo_tv.name: The Wasteland — Death Valley
fo_tv.description: Death Valley is aptly named in 2296. Radiation, Deathclaws, and wandering Ghoul bounty hunters make this stretch of desert one of the most lethal in the Western wasteland. And yet — traders still cross it, because the old Vault-Tec highway runs straight through the middle.

fo_tv.name: Moldaver's Fusion Power Station
fo_tv.description: Lee Moldaver's greatest achievement: a working cold fusion power station that HavenTech has spent decades trying to suppress. The station's energy grid runs on the same principles as the CAPS Protocol authentication system — limitless distributed power for limitless distributed currency.

fo_tv.name: The Prydwen Memorial — LA Ruins
fo_tv.description: The wreckage of a Brotherhood airship — whether the original Prydwen or a successor vessel — lies half-buried in the Los Angeles rubble. Brotherhood squires make pilgrimages here. Scribes recovered what they could from the tech. What they didn't take was a sealed CAPS Protocol terminal in the cargo bay.

fo_tv.name: Cooper Howard's Ranch — Pre-War Ruins
fo_tv.description: The ruins of Cooper Howard's pre-war ranch. Before the bombs, this was a working cattle ranch and film set. On October 22nd, 2077, Cooper Howard was filming a Nuka-Cola commercial here when his daughter called to warn him about the vaults. Now The Ghoul returns here sometimes, to remember.

fo_tv.name: Siggi Wilzig's Research Station
fo_tv.description: A converted pre-war research facility where Siggi Wilzig conducted his FizzCo experiments. Now his successor, Dr. Elara Voss, continues his work — including his most dangerous secret: documentation proving that the CAPS Protocol was designed for population control, not currency.

fo_tv.name: Lucy's Vault 33 Entrance
fo_tv.description: The exterior blast doors of Vault 33, where Lucy MacLean first stepped onto the surface. The ground outside is marked with old scorch patterns from the raiders' approach. Someone scratched 'THE OUTSIDE IS REAL' into the door frame in fresh letters.

fo_tv.name: Maximus's Power Armor Cache
fo_tv.description: A Brotherhood supply cache where Maximus resupplied during his assignment to retrieve the head of Siggi Wilzig. Multiple suits of T-60 armor, energy weapon cells, and — hidden in a false floor — a Brotherhood intelligence report on CAPS Protocol nodes embedded in civilian infrastructure.

fo_tv.name: The Gulch — Raider Stronghold
fo_tv.description: A natural canyon system that raiders have fortified into an impregnable stronghold. The Gulch's leadership collects CAPS from travelers — but not to trade. They're running CAPS Protocol authentication nodes, acting as unauthorized FIZZ minting operations. HavenTech wants them shut down.

fo_tv.name: HavenTech Headquarters Ruins
fo_tv.description: The corporate headquarters of HavenTech — Vault-Tec's surviving corporate successor. Abandoned after a catastrophic incident, the building is now a radioactive ruin guarded by malfunctioning security robots. Deep in the server room: the complete CAPS Protocol archive, including Vault 77's original source code.

fo_tv.name: Vault 31 — Norm's Cryosleep Vault
fo_tv.description: Vault 31: a vault where the most promising Vault-Tec executives were cryogenically preserved, waiting to be thawed when civilization was ready for them to lead it. Norm MacLean discovered what 'leadership' meant in Vault-Tec's vocabulary. The CAPS Protocol was always their plan — the vault experiment was the rehearsal.
